title: Scene runtime for generated visuals
acceptance: A v2 Current admits a generated scene { id, code }: an ES module with a default export of at most 24,576 bytes, refused with a path and a code otherwise or beside an engine; any cue name is the scene's to interpret; it lowers to a scene cue on the score and its cues to the scene's one command; unit-tested.

The scene's code runs only in a Web Worker that owns the transferred canvas, with every banned global shadowed by a stub that throws and cannot be put back before the code is imported; a dry frame runs before the scene is ready, and any error reports its phase, a bounded message and where in the scene's code; unit-tested against a fake worker scope.
In a host's card the worker is RISE's built script fetched as text and started from a blob: URL; the built worker imports nothing at run time (checked in dist).

The Chamber's runtime sends frames only while the reading plays (scene time stops on pause, a step is capped at 100 ms), fails a frame over 200 ms, three over 24 ms in one second, any reported error or a second of silence, then ends the worker and applies the reading's fallback, keeping a diagnostic; a scene that would flash more than three times a second is frozen; unit-tested.

A hold with maxMs under a scene that declared reportsCompletion ends when the scene says done, no sooner than 200 ms and no later than maxMs; otherwise, and on failure, at its ms; unit-tested at the runtime, the conductor and the live runtime.
In the self-contained card a generated scene draws and ends its hold early, and a scene that throws falls back with its hold at ms (e2e/live-mcp.spec.js).

evidence.note: The Creative Control design; §7 runtime, §8 scene API, §12 dry frame and fallback, §13 security.

activity.summary: Built on cc-004-manifests: worker, runtime, layer, score and compile, Chamber and conductor wiring, browser tests. Server static admission stays with CC-006; seek with instant cues and fonts in the worker are not built here.

summary: Generated scenes run in an isolated worker on the reading's clock, cued by beats, ending their holds, budgeted, flash-gated, and replaced by the reading's fallback when they fail.
